ticket.title: storypole update reports success but acceptance criteria do not persist
acceptance_criteria:
RETRACTED 2026-11-06 - this is NOT a product bug, it was my measurement error. update_task passes acceptance_criteria into a TaskUpdated event and record_event writes it; criteria persist correctly.

What I did wrong: I scanned the ledger for events whose embedded task snapshot carried ticket_key GB-250 and read that snapshot acceptance_criteria, which returned zero. But TaskUpdated events carry a delta keyed by task_id and embed NO task snapshot, so the last matching event was the creation record - a stale snapshot with no criteria on it. I was asking a question the data could not answer and treating the confident answer as fact.

Correct measurement, by task_id: 3 task_updated events exist for GB-250, the last carries 1 criterion, and its text preserved commas, backticks and double quotes exactly - which also proves --criterion-file works end to end (GB-250).

Lesson: when a verification returns zero, the first question is whether the query could have returned anything. Third time today I trusted a query whose shape did not match the data.

task.title: storypole update reports success but acceptance criteria do not persist

acceptance_criteria: GB-281 evidence: after `storypole update GB-250 --criterion-file /tmp/crit.txt` returned exit 0, the canonical ledger snapshot for GB-250 carries acceptance_criteria = []. The same snapshot shows none of the several criteria added to GB-250 earlier today through --criterion, which suggests persistence was already broken before --criterion-file existed - and that update has been reporting success while discarding criteria all session. Worth checking first: whether update_task applies Some(acceptance_criteria) at all, or whether the snapshot shape simply omits the field (in which case the earlier criteria are present and only the new one is missing). Cannot distinguish those two without reading update_task, which is the next step before any fix.
